sources.title: Simo Särkkä, Bayesian Filtering and Smoothing (2013)
sources.locator: Full 252-page author-hosted PDF retrieved. Inspected Chapter 7 §§7.3–7.5, PDF pp. 120–132; Chapter 11 §11.2, PDF pp. 167–169; §11.3, pp. 169–171; and §11.4, pp. 171–173, including SIS/SIR updates, Algorithm 7.6, Algorithm 11.2, the backward Bayes derivation, marginal recursion and the separate RBPS discussion.

contents.name: Chapter 7 §§7.3–7.4: weighted sequential importance sampling and SIR resampling procedure
contents.reason: These sections establish the weighted-particle and resampling setup. Their propagation-weight-resample ordering differs from the current batch-44 resample-propagate interface; the local induction follows that actual interface and proves its own limit.

contents.name: Chapter 7 §7.5: conditionally linear-Gaussian model factorization and Rao–Blackwellized filtering setup
contents.reason: The source identifies the conditionally Gaussian state and latent nonlinear path factorization; the local definition states the exact hierarchical model and covariance hypotheses used by this pair.

contents.name: Algorithm 7.6: conditional Kalman prediction, marginal observation likelihood, and Gaussian update per latent particle
contents.reason: This is the forward RBPF procedure. The local algorithm uses the bootstrap proposal specialization and explicitly retains finite-particle approximation limits.

contents.name: Chapter 11 §11.2: backward particle probabilities derived from the smoothing conditional density
contents.reason: The source's Bayes factorization is restated for declared reference measures, finite-positive predictive density, supplied fillers, and the general-kernel branch, then proved locally.

contents.name: Algorithm 11.2: terminal filtering draw followed by backward particle-index simulation
contents.reason: The local algorithm gives the exact normalized backward index weights and distinguishes them from recorded forward ancestors.

contents.name: Chapter 11 §§11.2–11.3: fixed-path and all-marginal operation counts
contents.reason: The source's O(SNT) path and O(N²T) all-marginal counts are proved by explicit loop counts under a stated unit-cost density-evaluation assumption.

contents.name: Chapter 11 §11.4: Rao–Blackwellized particle smoothing with conditional RTS passes
contents.reason: This is a separate smoothing algorithm that stores Gaussian histories and applies RTS smoothing; the controlling BCS-43 inventory assigns a forward Rao–Blackwellized particle filter, not this RBPS procedure.

sources.title: Arnaud Doucet and Adam M. Johansen, A Tutorial on Particle Filtering and Smoothing: Fifteen Years Later (2011)
sources.locator: Full 41-page PDF retrieved. Inspected §§3.4–3.5, PDF pp. 13–16; §2.3.1, pp. 7–8; §5.1, pp. 33–34; §5.2, pp. 34–36; and the start of §5.3, pp. 36–37, including multinomial resampling, the generic SMC order, backward formula, fixed-lag caveat and operation counts.

contents.name: §3.4: multinomial resampling as IID draws from normalized particle weights
contents.reason: This supports the conditional resampling law used by the local concentration proof. The source's generic SMC implementation resamples after proposal weighting, while the current BCS-41 algorithm resamples before propagation; the local proof explicitly uses the latter order.

contents.name: §3.5: generic sequential Monte Carlo procedure and its two weighted/resampled approximations
contents.reason: The source gives the generic SIS/resampling decomposition but uses a different operation order. It is recorded as context only; the local result is proved for the actual resample-propagate bootstrap supplier.

contents.name: §2.3.1: forward-backward factorization of the full smoothing path law
contents.reason: The source supports the Markov backward factorization; the local proof supplies the density and regular-conditional-kernel versions and exact null-set boundaries.

contents.name: §5.1: fixed-lag target p(x_t given observations only through t+L), with no generic fixed-L convergence to the full smoother
contents.reason: This matches the algorithm's truncated observation horizon. The local theorem proves its exact-kernel target and the example computes a nonzero finite lag bias.

contents.name: §5.2: particle approximation of the backward conditional and FFBSi path construction
contents.reason: The local procedure preserves the source formula while declaring its finite-positive denominator domain and the kernel-only alternative.

contents.name: §5.2: path-sampling versus all-marginal operation counts
contents.reason: The source reports linear-in-N cost for a fixed number of paths and quadratic-in-N cost for all marginal pairs; the local theorem proves both by counting evaluations.

contents.name: §5.3: generalized two-filter formula and a distinct backward filtering algorithm
contents.reason: This is a separate two-filter particle method and is not among the controlling BCS-43 claims or item inventory.

sources.title: Fredrik Lindsten, Pete Bunch, Simo Särkkä, Thomas B. Schön, and Simon J. Godsill, Rao-Blackwellized Particle Smoothers for Conditionally Linear Gaussian Models (2016)
sources.locator: Full 29-page arXiv PDF retrieved. Inspected §3.1, PDF pp. 4–5, and §3.2, pp. 5–6, including the particle-path approximation, conditional Gaussian mixture and RBPF likelihood-weight contract.

contents.name: §3.2: particle approximation of the nonlinear path marginal with one conditional Kalman Gaussian per particle
contents.reason: This independently supports the finite Gaussian-mixture representation; exact conditional moments are justified by the locally checked Kalman supplier rather than by the paper's informal presentation.

contents.name: §3.2: conditional Gaussian moments along a fixed nonlinear path
contents.reason: The article supplies context for the conditional Kalman components, while the local lemma proves the exact statement from the current Kalman-filter supplier and its stated innovation hypotheses.

contents.name: §3.1: forward particle approximation of a state-space smoothing path law
contents.reason: The source motivates reducing path degeneracy by backward simulation; the exact backward kernel and finite-particle limits are separately proved or stated in the local carriers.

alternatives.argument: The local proof forms the conditional pair law eta_t(dx) f_{t+1}(x'|x) lambda(dx'), applies the retrieved conditional-density theorem on finite-positive predictive-density fibers, cancels future Markov factors, and iterates the resulting backward RCDs to recover the smoothing path kernel. The no-density case uses a supplied backward conditional kernel.

The local algorithm specifies terminal filtering-weight sampling, derives each particle-index probability by normalizing w_t^i f(x'|x_t^i), rejects zero or infinite denominators, gives an exact supplied-kernel branch, and separately defines the all-marginal recursion.

The local algorithm runs backward only to s=min(t+L,T) and states its exact-kernel target as the conditional law given observations through s. The finite-state B example proves that this target can differ from the full smoother.

The local proof first proves a bootstrap filter weak law under compact state spaces, Feller transitions, multinomial resampling, and bounded positive continuous potentials. It then proves uniform convergence of backward kernels by finite nets on compact spaces, composes finitely many kernels, and controls the S_N trajectory Monte Carlo error by the Chebyshev-Markov integral inequality.
